s: Der Tod kam endlich zu ihm her.
Tod.et: From Middle High German tōt, from Old High German tōd, from Proto-West Germanic *dauþu, from Proto-Germanic *dauþuz. Compare Old Saxon dōth, Dutch dood, English death, Danish død.

s: Es gab vier Todesfälle beim Unglück.
There were four deaths in the accident.
angel of death (a personification of death)

Todestrieb.et: Coined by Sigmund Freud, Tod + -es- + Trieb

s: death row cell; cell in a prison in which a person who has been sentenced to death is held
day of someone's death, date on which someone will die
Bis zu seinem Todestag engagierte er sich für die Armen.
He advocated for the poor until the day he died.
Todestag.et: From Tod + -es- + Tag. Compare Swedish dödsdag and English deathday, which are formed similarly.

s: a longing or yearning for death, be it conscious or subconscious
Death Valley (a valley in eastern California, the lowest point in North America)
Ich sehe eine Weile hin, und dann merke ich, daß Rollo neben mir weint. Ich meine, ich habe natürlich geahnt, daß Rollo todtraurig ist die ganze Zeit.
The rune ᛦ (Yr), symbolizing death according to Ariosophy.

Es handele sich um die auch von den Nazis verwendete Todesrune, oder zumindest um die auf den Kopf gestellte Algiz-Rune, die mit stilisiertem Astwerk oder wahlweise den Hörnern des Elchs das Leben symbolisiert.
Die Homepage der Nordischen Zeitung zieren eine Todesrune und ein Gedicht in Fraktur: "Besitz stirbt, Sippen sterben / Du selbst stirbst wie sie / eins weiß ich, das ewig lebt / der Toten Totenruhm".
»Die Todesspirale aus Klimakipppunkten beginnt sich bereits zu drehen und keine der Parteien hat einen Plan, das noch in den Griff zu bekommen«, kommentierte die Protestgruppe ihre Aktionen.
death squad (armed group carrying out extrajudicial killings, often in the form of massacres)
Todesschwadron.et: From Tod + -es- + Schwadron. Contemporary use probably after English death squad. Occasionally attested before the 20th century in the sense “suicide squad” (formation executing a highly risky command).

Todesgruppe.et: Calque of Spanish grupo de la muerte. By surface analysis, Tod + -es- + Gruppe.

s: death, a fate that decrees one’s end
a draw (seeding) in a tournament by which some competitor is seeded against one of the strongest opponents and thus likely to be eliminated
Todeslos.et: From Tod (“death”) + -es- + Los (“lot”). The sports sense after Todesgruppe.

s: Todtnau (a town in southern Baden-Württemberg, Germany)
A literary device, somewhat common in ancient epic, consisting of a chain of deaths in which one warrior is killed by another, who is in turn killed by a third, and so forth.
the fact that a crime results in the unintended death of the victim, by negligence or (certain forms of) recklessness
death driver (a person who deliberately rams a vehicle into a group of people)
danger of death, deadly danger, mortal danger
one condemned to death, dead man walking, goner
